method: Exploratory, unblinded qualitative inspection of the retained public continuations. No independent raters, semantic judge, or statistical coherence score. All planned outputs are retained, including failures.
shakespeare: Standard continuation improves both reserved-text likelihood and external Hamlet likelihood and removes artificial paragraph markers in these samples. Individual fragments are more conventional, but broken grammar, invented words and abrupt speaker/topic changes remain. Unlikelihood lowers token repetition yet increases word repetition versus standard continuation; it is not a general quality win.
architecture: Both revised runs improve held-out prediction within the matched step budget. The generated samples still show malformed grammar, generic dialogue and weak prompt/speaker continuity. This supports better learning efficiency on the tested corpus, not dependable coherence.
stories: The first-budget model produces more conventional everyday sentences and usually stops at a story boundary. However, every one of the 16 inspected continuations has a clear entity, topic or causal failure. It changes names, replaces objects and misses simple counting. Word repetition averages 1.78%; a lower-loss story model is not yet a reliably coherent storyteller.

chat: Continuing the original chat model produced only a tiny historical-test change: 1.3708 to 1.3697 bits/byte with standard likelihood, or 1.3695 with unlikelihood (about 0.1%). Both selected additional step 600. This is too small and too historically entangled to claim a meaningful improvement in conversational coherence; no private chat samples or independent ratings were used.
story_continuation: The further-trained model lowers bits/byte on the new common reserved slice from 0.7528 to 0.6934 (7.9%). Average repeated word 4-grams fall from 1.78% to 1.44% across the same 16 continuations. Several outputs stay on the local topic better: both soup prompts now remain about soup, and the first lost-dog continuation keeps the dog and girl. However, every reviewed continuation still contains an entity, goal or causal failure. Object tracking, counting and consistent names remain unreliable. These are modest topic/prediction gains, not a solved coherence problem.
